translation_notes: the coercion_datatype sites are four `rdflib.term.Literal(value, lang=...)` calls on computed strings, each with a LITERAL (source-constant) language tag -- unlike the sibling region Concept._add_subject_to_graph, where the tag itself is a runtime value, here the tag is always known at translation time (u'en'/u'lv' hard-coded at each call site), so the language's dedicated `{expr}@lang` notation applies directly: `Literal(termEN, lang=u'en')` -> `{termEN}@en`

topic_node = eliozo:{"TRM-" + conceptID}: original.py builds the IRI by plain string concatenation (eliozo_ns + "TRM-" + conceptID), never percent-encoding conceptID -- ex:{expr} matches that exactly (concatenates, does not encode). Not translated as e<eliozo_ns/TRM-{?id}> (which would percent-encode) since that would change behaviour for a conceptID containing a space or slash -- no such guarantee is visible in this region alone

rdf:type / RDF_NS: translated with the Turtle `a` shortcut (`+{ {topic_node} a eliozo:Concept }`) rather than declaring an @prefix rdf: only to spell out rdf:type -- no @prefix rdf: is declared since nothing in the translated body dereferences it (RDF_NS, a plain Python string constant, not a Namespace object, is left unused at module level, same as in original.py's own dead `rdf_type_property` local before this translation)

the three .add() calls that share `topic_node` as subject (termEN/termLV/conceptID) are combined into one +{ s p1 o1 ; p2 o2 ; p3 o3 } predicate-object list, per INSTRUCTIONS.md's add_run_shared_subject row -- this is the direct Turtle reading of three .add() calls on the same subject, not a restructuring: no reordering, no merged logic, same five triples either way

the rdf:type add and the conditional descLV add are kept as their own separate +{ } islands (not folded into the shared-subject block): the former precedes termEN's fallback computation in program order, the latter is conditional -- folding either in would change what depends on what, or write into the graph a triple the original's guard would have skipped

@graph g: `g` (the function parameter) is never reassigned in this region's body, only added to, so `@graph g` at the top of the function captures a graph reference that stays valid for the whole call -- see INSTRUCTIONS.md's warning about `@graph` capturing a value, not a name, for the case where that would not hold

anti-hollow-green (INSTRUCTIONS.md): changed eliozo:termLV's language tag from @lv to @en in translated.ldpy -- rdfeval check correctly failed on all three calls (graphs not isomorphic, 5 vs 5 / 4 vs 4 / 4 vs 4 triples); reverted, check green again
